title: The connection nobody missed
paragraphs: When their first flight landed late, Priya and her colleague assumed they had missed their connection. The departure screen showed that the next plane was still on time, but its gate was on the other side of the terminal. They had twenty minutes, and Priya's colleague suggested running straight there. Priya wanted to speak to an airline employee first. Her colleague thought this would waste the few minutes they had left.

The employee checked their boarding passes and explained that the connecting flight was waiting for several passengers from the late arrival. However, she also noticed that their checked luggage had been booked to a different airport in the same city. Running to the gate would not have solved that problem. She called the baggage team, corrected the destination, and gave the passengers a printed confirmation.

They reached the gate while the last group was boarding. On the plane, Priya's colleague admitted that stopping had been the better decision. Priya was less certain. If the employee had not been available, she might have chosen differently. What mattered, she said, was asking the right person rather than simply moving faster. When they arrived, both suitcases were on the correct baggage carousel. Their meeting was the following morning, so they still had the evening to prepare.

questions.question: Why did the colleague want to run?
options: He wanted to leave Priya behind
The employee told him to run
He believed very little boarding time remained
He knew the baggage was at the wrong airport
questions.evidence: They had twenty minutes
questions.explanation: Początkowa decyzja wynikała z małej ilości czasu, nie z wiedzy o bagażu.

questions.question: What unexpected problem did the employee find?
options: The connecting flight had already left
The bags had the wrong destination airport
The passengers had no passports
The meeting had been canceled
questions.evidence: their checked luggage had been booked to a different airport in the same city.
questions.explanation: Błąd dotyczył miejsca docelowego bagażu, a nie bramki pasażerów.

questions.question: What does Priya suggest about her decision?
options: It depended on getting useful help quickly
Stopping is always better than running
Airline employees never make mistakes
Passengers should ignore departure screens
questions.evidence: If the employee had not been available, she might have chosen differently.
questions.explanation: Priya nie tworzy uniwersalnej reguły: uwzględnia dostępność pomocy.

questions.question: Which outcome is supported by the passage?
options: They reached the meeting late
Only one suitcase arrived
The plane waited only for them
They caught the flight and received their bags
questions.evidence: both suitcases were on the correct baggage carousel.
questions.explanation: Dotarli na lot i odebrali oba bagaże; samolot czekał na kilka osób.

title: A quieter kind of success
paragraphs: A neighborhood restaurant introduced a special lunch menu to attract office workers. The owner, Rosa, expected customers to care mainly about speed and price. For the first week, the kitchen prepared three dishes in advance, and the staff promised that every meal would reach the table within ten minutes. Sales increased, but several customers left without ordering. Rosa assumed the menu was too limited.

Instead of immediately adding more dishes, she asked people near the entrance why they were leaving. Some had only wanted a coffee, but others said the music made conversation difficult. One customer regularly met a client over lunch and needed somewhere quiet. Rosa lowered the volume in the back room and stopped seating large groups there. She kept the same lunch menu and prices.

A month later, the quieter tables were usually full. Meals there took slightly longer because customers stayed to talk, so those tables served fewer people each afternoon. Even so, the restaurant earned more from the room because guests often ordered desserts and returned the following week. Rosa kept the faster service at the front for customers with short breaks. The result did not show that speed was unimportant. It showed that different customers used the same restaurant for different reasons, and one arrangement could not satisfy them all.

questions.question: What did Rosa first think was wrong?
options: The staff were cooking too slowly
There were not enough menu choices
The music was too quiet
The prices had increased
questions.evidence: Rosa assumed the menu was too limited.
questions.explanation: To była pierwsza hipoteza właścicielki, później zmieniona po rozmowach.

questions.question: What did she change after asking customers?
options: The atmosphere in part of the restaurant
Every dish on the menu
All the prices
The opening hours
questions.evidence: Rosa lowered the volume in the back room
questions.explanation: Zmieniła warunki rozmowy, pozostawiając menu i ceny.

questions.question: Why did the back room earn more despite serving fewer people?
options: Every meal cost twice as much
All customers stopped talking
The kitchen hired fewer people
Guests bought extra items and returned
questions.evidence: guests often ordered desserts and returned the following week.
questions.explanation: Większe wydatki i powroty klientów zrównoważyły mniejszą liczbę obsłużonych osób.

questions.question: What is the main lesson?
options: Office workers dislike low prices
Restaurants should never change menus
Different needs may require different arrangements
Fast service always reduces profits
questions.evidence: different customers used the same restaurant for different reasons
questions.explanation: Wniosek dotyczy różnych potrzeb, a nie całkowitego odrzucenia szybkości obsługi.

title: The repair that took two Saturdays
paragraphs: Lena took an old radio to a volunteer repair club. It had belonged to her grandfather, and she hoped to use it in her kitchen. At the entrance, a sign warned visitors that volunteers could not promise to repair every object. They would also ask owners to stay and help rather than simply leave their things and return later. Lena had expected a free repair service, so this surprised her.

A volunteer named Marcus showed her how to open the case safely. They found a damaged switch, but the club did not have a replacement. Lena offered to buy a new radio and give up on the old one. Marcus explained that a suitable switch would be inexpensive, although finding the right size might take time. He wrote down the measurements, and Lena ordered the part that evening.

The following Saturday, they fitted the switch together. The radio worked, but the sound was still not perfect. Marcus offered to investigate further. Lena decided it was good enough for the kitchen and took it home. She had spent more time than she expected, but she now understood how to check a simple fault. A month later, she returned with a broken lamp and the correct replacement cable. This time, she brought her younger brother because he wanted to learn too.

questions.question: How was the club different from Lena's expectation?
options: Owners took part in the repairs
Every repair was guaranteed
Only new objects were accepted
Visitors had to work there every week
questions.evidence: ask owners to stay and help
questions.explanation: Klub angażował właścicieli, zamiast wyłącznie wykonywać usługę za nich.

questions.question: Why was a second visit necessary?
options: Marcus forgot the appointment
The radio needed a new case
Lena had not brought the radio
The correct switch was not available
questions.evidence: the club did not have a replacement.
questions.explanation: Brak części wymusił zamówienie i ponowną wizytę.

questions.question: Was the radio completely perfect when Lena took it home?
options: No, and it could not produce sound
Yes, because she bought a new one
No, but it met her needs
Yes, Marcus replaced every part
questions.evidence: Lena decided it was good enough for the kitchen
questions.explanation: Działało wystarczająco dobrze; tekst zaznacza niedoskonały dźwięk.

questions.question: What does Lena's later visit suggest?
options: She had become a paid electrician
She had gained confidence and wanted to share the experience
She believed volunteers should do all the work
She no longer wanted to repair anything
questions.evidence: she returned with a broken lamp and the correct replacement cable.
questions.explanation: Przygotowała część samodzielnie i przyprowadziła brata; nie ma mowy o zdobyciu zawodu.

title: The shorter route
paragraphs: Four friends planned a long walk through the hills. They had studied a map and chosen a route that usually took five hours. The weather forecast showed light rain in the morning and sunshine later. Because everyone wanted to reach a small village for lunch, they agreed to leave early. By nine o'clock, however, they were still at the station: one train had been canceled, and the next was crowded.

When they finally arrived at the start of the trail, Noah suggested taking a shorter route. It would miss the highest viewpoint but pass an old bridge and reach the village before the cafe closed. The others were disappointed. They had looked forward to the view, and the sky was now clear. One friend argued that they could walk faster and still complete the original route.

Noah pointed out that walking faster would leave little time for breaks. They had different levels of fitness, and the last bus home would not wait for them. After checking the map again, the group chose the shorter path. They reached the village comfortably and even had time to talk to the cafe owner about local history. On the bus home, they agreed to attempt the longer route another day. Changing the plan had not been their first choice, but it had kept the afternoon enjoyable for everyone.

questions.question: What mainly caused the change of plan?
options: Heavy rain all day
The bridge being closed
A lost map
A transport delay
questions.evidence: one train had been canceled
questions.explanation: Zdecydowało opóźnienie dojazdu; podczas rozmowy o trasie niebo było już czyste.

questions.question: What would they miss on the shorter route?
options: The village
The cafe
The highest viewpoint
The old bridge
questions.evidence: It would miss the highest viewpoint but pass an old bridge
questions.explanation: Krótsza trasa pomijała punkt widokowy, lecz prowadziła przez most i wieś.

questions.question: Why did Noah reject simply walking faster?
options: The map did not show distances
The group had different abilities and a fixed return time
Nobody wanted lunch
He had already seen the village
questions.evidence: They had different levels of fitness, and the last bus home would not wait for them.
questions.explanation: Łączył potrzeby uczestników z ograniczeniem czasowym autobusu.

questions.question: How did the friends feel about the final choice?
options: They accepted it as a good adjustment
They decided never to walk again
They regretted speaking to the cafe owner
They believed the long route was impossible
questions.evidence: it had kept the afternoon enjoyable for everyone.
questions.explanation: Nie był to plan pierwotny, ale pozwolił wszystkim przyjemnie spędzić czas.

title: A question before opening
paragraphs: On his first morning at a bookstore, Ethan was asked to prepare an online order. The customer had bought a travel guide and a notebook. Ethan found both items and was about to wrap them when he noticed that the guide described the previous year's train schedules. A newer edition stood on the same shelf, but it cost more. The order clearly named the older edition.

Ethan could have followed the order exactly and finished the task quickly. Instead, he asked his supervisor whether they should contact the customer. She said that some customers deliberately bought older guides because they were cheaper, while others did not realize there was a difference. She helped Ethan write a short message explaining both options without recommending the more expensive book automatically.

The customer replied before the shop opened. She was collecting old editions for a research project and wanted the exact book she had ordered. Ethan wrapped it and added a note confirming the edition. His question had not led to a different sale, but the supervisor was pleased. The aim, she explained, was not always to change a customer's mind. Sometimes checking an unusual detail was simply a way to make sure the shop had understood the request. Later that week, Ethan noticed a similar issue in another order and knew whom to ask.

questions.question: What made Ethan hesitate?
options: The customer had not paid
The shop had no newer guide
The guide contained old schedules
The notebook was missing
questions.evidence: the guide described the previous year's train schedules.
questions.explanation: Wątpliwość dotyczyła aktualności przewodnika, nie braku produktu.

questions.question: What did the supervisor recommend?
options: Send the expensive guide for free
Explain the options without assuming what the customer wanted
Always sell the latest edition
Cancel the order immediately
questions.evidence: explaining both options without recommending the more expensive book automatically.
questions.explanation: Chodziło o sprawdzenie potrzeby klientki, a nie automatyczne zwiększenie sprzedaży.

questions.question: Why did the customer want the old guide?
options: She was doing research
She could not afford any newer books
She was leaving by train that day
She had not seen the year
questions.evidence: She was collecting old editions for a research project
questions.explanation: Wybór starszego wydania był świadomy i związany z badaniami.

questions.question: Why was the supervisor pleased?
options: Ethan sold a more expensive book
The customer canceled the order
The task took no time
Ethan checked that the request was understood
questions.evidence: make sure the shop had understood the request.
questions.explanation: Sukcesem było upewnienie się, że zamówienie odpowiada intencji klientki.
